page: Amazon Web Services m9g.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton Gen9 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture using Neoverse-V3 cores, this instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at 3.3 GHz. It features 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local NVMe storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, alongside top-tier Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. Passmark memory and database operations also rank in the top tier, while Redis SET operations demonstrate strong performance at 92.33 million operations per second. However, LLM inference tasks show mixed results, with weak text generation speeds for small models, though prompt processing remains average. The lack of local storage and dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy storage-bound or hardware-accelerated machine learning workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARMv9 architecture delivers high resource density and strong performance per watt, making it an efficient option for general-purpose workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. The instance is well-suited for software compilation, database operations, static web serving, text processing, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks.

It features 32 dedicated physical cores, 128.0 GB of RAM, and a 17 Gbps baseline network speed, running on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show top-tier capabilities in software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and single-threaded compression, alongside strong multi-core processing. However, LLM text generation performance is relatively weak. This instance offers a highly resource-dense, cost-efficient profile for general-purpose workloads, making it suitable for multi-threaded applications, web serving, and database management.
